Nobody tells you this: five days decided the whole year in the Nifty.
Say you put one lakh rupees in the Nifty fifty a year ago, on fourth November twenty twenty five. Today it's worth about ninety three thousand. Down seven percent.
Now say you got scared, and stayed out on just the five best days. Five, out of two hundred forty six. How much is left? Guess before the timer ends.
Eighty two thousand, eight hundred. A seven percent loss became seventeen. But here's the strange part nobody tells you.
When did the best day of the year come? In a calm, happy market? Or right after a crash? Three. Two. One.
Right after the crash. On eighth April, the Nifty jumped almost four percent, just over a week after one of its worst falls of the year.
And it's not a one off. Four of the five best days came within two weeks of one of the ten worst days. The bounce comes when fear is highest.
So here's the lesson. You can't dodge the worst days without missing the best ones. Staying invested beat jumping in and out. Past data, not a promise.
